title: Presenting data quiz
description: Ten questions drawn at random from a bank of thirteen, covering frequency polygons, stem-and-leaf diagrams, scatter graphs and choosing graphs.

questions.prompt: Where do you plot the point for the class $10 \le t < 15$ with frequency 8 on a frequency polygon?
questions.explanation: At the midpoint of the class, at the height of the frequency.

questions.prompt: Apples: frequencies 2, 15, 45, 27, 7, 4. How many apples were weighed?
The points of a frequency polygon are joined with a smooth curve.
questions.explanation: False — they are joined with straight lines.

questions.prompt: In a back-to-back stem-and-leaf diagram with key $1 \mid 7 = 17$ on the right, how do you read the left-hand leaves $5\;3 \mid 4$?

options.text: 45 and 43 — the order does not matter

questions.explanation: The left leaves read outwards from the stem: 43 then 45. (Without a key for the left you cannot be sure of place value — always include one.)
Eight values: the median is halfway between the 4th (17) and 5th (19), which is 18.

questions.prompt: For the ages 12, 15, 15, 17, 19, 22, 22, 22, find the mode and the range.
What correlation would you expect between the age of a car and its value?
questions.explanation: As cars get older, their value generally goes down.

questions.prompt: Click the **outlier** on this scatter graph of revision hours against test score.
questions.explanation: $(6, 30)$ is far below the upward trend — perhaps that student was ill on the day.

questions.prompt: A line of best fit must pass through the origin.
questions.explanation: False. It follows the trend of the points, wherever that is.

questions.prompt: In a pie chart for 40 people, how many degrees represent 12 people?
Which graph is best for showing how a baby's mass changes month by month?
questions.explanation: A trend over time is best shown on a line graph.

questions.prompt: A bar chart's $y$-axis starts at 90 instead of 0. What is the effect?

options.text: Small differences between bars look much bigger

questions.explanation: Cutting off the baseline exaggerates differences; the data itself is unchanged.

options.text: Correlation does not prove that one variable causes the other
Strong correlation means the points lie close to a straight line
A scatter graph showing no correlation must have been drawn wrongly
A line of best fit can be used to estimate values within the data range

questions.explanation: No correlation is a perfectly valid result — it tells you there is no link.
